items.stem: A formula suddenly shows #REF!. The most likely cause is:

options.text: A cell or range the formula referred to was deleted
options.rationale: Correct: #REF! appears when a reference becomes invalid, often after a delete.

items.explanation: Correct: #REF! indicates an invalid reference, typically because a referenced cell or range was deleted.

items.stem: Which TWO are Excel formula-auditing tools? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: Trace Precedents highlights cells feeding a formula.
Correct: Evaluate Formula steps through a calculation.
Freeze Panes is a view aid, not an auditing tool.
A printing view, not an auditing tool.

items.explanation: Correct: Trace Precedents and Evaluate Formula are auditing tools; the others are view or print aids.

items.stem: What is the risk of wrapping every formula in IFERROR by default?

options.text: It can mask genuine errors that should be investigated and fixed
options.rationale: Correct: blanket IFERROR hides the cause instead of fixing it.

options.text: It makes the workbook calculate faster
options.rationale: Speed is not the concern here.
IFERROR does not change data types by itself.
